---
title: "6.7 Limitations and compensating controls"
order: 7
---

The chapter raises five open findings about the tool and its inputs. Each has evidence
drawn from the facts or the code, a compensating control and an owner. The same five, in
the same words, are D6's open findings in the validation sign-off (D11, in the validation
PDF). The engine and the assumptions are not changed by this chapter: it documents them as
committed.

None of the findings is an error in the arithmetic, which holds on every loan
([6.5](performance.qmd#pr-identities)). They are about what the tool's output means, what
it leaves out, what is untested, and who governs its inputs.

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |

## Finding 1 — The headline mispricing share measures the generator's quotes {#pr-finding-1}

**Finding.** Most of the booked book misses the hurdle at its quoted rate. That is not
evidence about how a bank prices: it is a consequence of how the data generator built the
quotes, together with the difference between the PD the quotes were built on and the PD the
engine uses.

**Evidence.** The quoted rate, `risk_based_rate`, is set in `shared/data_generator.py`:

```python
risk_based_rate = (                                     # shared/data_generator.py
    MARKET["cost_of_funds"]
    + pd_true * MARKET["lgd"]
    + MARKET["opex_rate"]
    + MARKET["base_margin"]
    + rng.normal(0.0, 0.003, n)
).round(4)
```

That is break-even ([6.3](methodology.qmd#pr-break-even)) at the generator's true PD, plus
the base margin, plus noise. The engine's hurdle-clearing rate is break-even at the
scorecard's PD plus the capital charge ([6.3](methodology.qmd#pr-hurdle-clearing)). Subtract
one from the other and the cost of funds and operating cost cancel:

```
quoted − hurdle_clearing = (true PD − score PD) × lgd + noise − (capital charge − base_margin)
```

The capital charge, `roe_hurdle × capital_ratio / (1 − tax_rate)`, is
{{< var pricing.capital_charge >}}; the base margin is {{< var market.base_margin >}}; the
last term is therefore {{< var pricing.capital_charge_less_margin >}}
([6.4](assumptions.qmd#pr-capital-charge)). So, apart from the rounding of the quote to four
decimal places, a loan clears only where the true PD exceeds the scorecard's by enough, or
the noise is large enough, to make up that gap. On the committed data,
{{< var pricing.n_mispriced >}} of the {{< var pricing.n >}} booked loans
({{< var pricing.share_mispriced >}}) do not.

This page quotes the generator's code, not its truth: no figure in this chapter is computed
from the generator's true PD (the only place facts may use it is the ceiling in D4). The
argument needs only the code and the market facts.

**Impact.** The level of the headline — {{< var pricing.share_mispriced >}} mispriced,
\${{< var pricing.mispriced_ead >}} of EAD — is set by the generator's choice to quote without
a capital charge. A reader who takes it as a finding about pricing discipline is reading a
property of synthetic data. Two things are still valid: the arithmetic, and the measure
itself, which does exactly what [6.1](purpose.qmd) says. What the share does carry is a
second, real lesson: a quote built on information the bank's scorecard does not have (here,
the true PD) can only be judged against the scorecard's view, and part of what the measure
reports is the gap between the two views — which is also why the quoted rate is on the
leakage deny-list for models ([6.2](data.qmd#pr-quoted-rate)).

**Compensating control.** Wherever the mispriced share is shown — the portal, this
documentation, the workshop material — present it as a demonstration of the measure on
generated quotes, not as a finding about a book; this record and the prohibited use in
[6.1](purpose.qmd#prohibited-uses) are the control today. Before any use on real loans,
measure against the rates the bank actually quoted, and re-derive the share before acting on
it ([D1](../d1-purpose.qmd#prohibited-uses)). **Owner:** pricing tool owner (proposed; to be named).

The session video below calls the mispriced EAD, \${{< var pricing.mispriced_ead >}}, "below
the hurdle". It still teaches how the waterfall and the hurdle test work, and that a quote can
only be judged against the bank's own PD; it does not show a pricing practice, because the
generator quotes without the capital charge (finding 1).

{{< yt S3-c4 >}}

## Finding 2 — Loss-making loans are not separated from loans that miss the hurdle {#pr-finding-2}

**Finding.** The verdict is one flag: a loan clears the hurdle or it is mispriced. A loan
one basis point short and a loan that loses money at its own quote carry the same flag, and
the tool's summary reports nothing that tells them apart.

**Evidence.** Over the booked book ([6.5](performance.qmd#pr-headline)):
{{< var pricing.below_break_even.n >}} loans ({{< var pricing.below_break_even.share >}}),
with \${{< var pricing.below_break_even.ead >}} of EAD, are quoted below their break-even
rate; the facts assert they are exactly the {{< var pricing.negative_roe.n >}} loans with
negative ROE. `portfolio_summary` returns `n`, `n_clears`, `share_clears`, `median_roe`,
`mispriced_ead` and the mispriced share by band and by industry: no break-even count and no
break-even EAD. The v1 portal serves that summary; the v2 workbench shows a loan's break-even
rate on its rate ladder, one loan at a time. The book-level break-even figures in this
chapter come from the facts, not from the tool.

**Impact.** The summary understates the most actionable part of its own result. Missing the
hurdle is a question of return on capital; pricing below break-even is a loss on every such
loan, before any capital is charged. A reader of the portal's summary sees
{{< var pricing.share_mispriced >}} mispriced and cannot tell how much of it is loss-making.
On this data the level is set by the generator (finding 1); the gap in the summary would be
the same on a real book.

**Compensating control.** Report the below-break-even count and EAD beside the mispriced
share: the facts recompute both through the engine's `break_even_rate` on every `verify.py`
run, and the monitoring plan tracks them ([6.8](monitoring.qmd)). At the next change to
`pricing/`, add both to `portfolio_summary`, so that the portal shows them too.
**Owner:** pricing tool owner (proposed; to be named).

## Finding 3 — In bands AAA to B the rates rest on a PD that under-predicts {#pr-finding-3}

**Finding.** In bands AAA, A and B, D4 finds the scorecard's PD below the observed default
rate on the loans the bank books. The engine's hurdle-clearing and recommended rates for
those loans are built on that PD, so they rest on the weakest part of its input, in the
direction of being too low. The same bands show the highest mispriced share; that
concentration is a product of finding 1's construction, not of the PD.

**Evidence.** By score band, over the booked book ([6.5](performance.qmd#pr-by-band)):
band AAA {{< var pricing.band.AAA.mispriced_rate >}} mispriced
({{< var pricing.band.AAA.n >}} loans), band A {{< var pricing.band.A.mispriced_rate >}}
({{< var pricing.band.A.n >}}), against the lowest, band {{< var pricing.best_band >}}, at
{{< var pricing.best_band_rate >}}. On the scorecard's held-out booked applicants
([D4.5](../score/performance.qmd#held-out-booked-applicants)), observed default over mean
predicted PD is {{< var score.band_booked.B.ratio >}} in band B, on
{{< var score.band_booked.B.defaults >}} defaults — D4 finding 6, which clears the monitoring
floor of {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} defaults — and
{{< var score.band_booked.A.ratio >}} in band A and {{< var score.band_booked.AAA.ratio >}}
in band AAA, on {{< var score.band_booked.A.defaults >}} and
{{< var score.band_booked.AAA.defaults >}} defaults, below the floor and so D4 observations,
not findings. All three are above the tolerance's upper edge,
{{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}}: more default than the PD predicts. The pattern is the same
one D5 finds in its own model's Approve zone (D5 finding 3), under-prediction where risk
looks low; pricing takes the scorecard's PD, not D5's, so only D4's evidence reaches the rate.

What the two facts do and do not say together:

- **Under-prediction does not cause the concentration.** A PD that is too low makes the
  hurdle-clearing rate too low, which makes a loan *more* likely to clear, not less. Reading
  the generator's code, we would expect the concentration from finding 1's construction: where
  PD × LGD is small, little stands between the quote and the
  {{< var pricing.capital_charge_less_margin >}} gap ([6.5](performance.qmd#pr-by-band)). That
  is a reading of the code, consistent with the table, not a measured decomposition.
- **The AAA calibration miss is probably noise.** Read through finding 1's algebra, if the true AAA
  default rate were {{< var score.band_booked.AAA.ratio >}} times its PD, the typical AAA quote
  would sit above the gap and most AAA loans would clear; instead
  {{< var pricing.band.AAA.mispriced_rate >}} are mispriced. That supports D4's treatment of the
  AAA miss, on {{< var score.band_booked.AAA.defaults >}} defaults, as an observation, not a
  finding.
- **It does mean the measured shortfall there is, if anything, too small,** and the
  recommended rates too low. D4 finding 6 says it of band B in so many words: band B loans
  are priced too cheaply.

**Impact.** In bands AAA to B the recommended and hurdle-clearing rates are least reliable,
in the direction of being too low; band B, where D4's evidence clears the floor, most of all. A price floor or a
rate card set from the recommended rates in bands AAA to B would inherit that. Band D, by
contrast, carries the most mispriced exposure (\${{< var pricing.band.D.mispriced_ead >}})
on a PD that D4 finds inside the tolerance on all held-out applicants
({{< var score.band.D.ratio >}}) and on the held-out booked ({{< var score.band_booked.D.ratio >}}).

**Compensating control.** When D4 finding 6's control is applied — a recalibration of band B,
or an overlay on its PD — re-run pricing and re-read [6.5](performance.qmd) and
[6.6](sensitivity.qmd). Until then, monitor the mispriced share and EAD by band beside D4's
band calibration on the booked ([6.8](monitoring.qmd)), and do not set a band's price floor
from the engine's recommended rates in bands AAA to B. **Owner:** pricing tool owner (proposed; to be
named), with the model developer (D4).

## Finding 4 — The fee and the book-level functions are untested {#pr-finding-4}

**Finding.** Two parts of the code the portal relies on have no test of their own: the
engine with a non-zero fee, and the two functions that price and summarise the book.

**Evidence.**

- **`fee_rate`.** It is a field of `MarketAssumptions` with a default of
  {{< var pricing.fee_rate >}}, and it is not in `MARKET`, so the batch never sets it. It
  enters interest income and is subtracted in the break-even and hurdle-clearing rates
  ([6.3](methodology.qmd)). None of the {{< var pricing.n_engine_tests >}} tests in
  `tests/test_engine.py` sets it. The workbench tests send it only at its default, and the one
  test that moves it is the facts' own check, added with this chapter as the interim control
  below.
  Yet the v2 what-if accepts it (`PricingOverrides.fee_rate`, from 0 to 1) and the
  workbench's pricing tab has a slider for it.
- **`price_population` and `portfolio_summary`.** No test calls either directly to check its
  behaviour. They are exercised indirectly: the portal runs them at start-up, so the portal
  and workbench tests use their output; the facts tests pin their result against the
  committed summary; and `verify.py` compares the live summary with the committed one
  ([6.9](gate.qmd)). The notebook test only checks that a notebook cell calls
  `price_population`.

**Impact.** The engine's identities are pinned on one loan with no fee; a defect that only
appears with a fee — a sign error, a fee counted twice — would reach the workbench untested.
A defect in the book-level functions that left the three compared summary figures within
tolerance would pass `verify.py`. Neither is known to exist: the identities hold with a fee
on every booked loan ([6.5](performance.qmd#pr-identities)), and the summary matches. The
finding is that nothing *designed* to catch them is in place.

**Compensating control.** At the next change to `pricing/`, add an engine test at a non-zero
fee (break-even and hurdle identities, and the fee's effect on interest income) and unit tests
of `price_population` and `portfolio_summary` on a small fixed book. Until then, the facts
re-check both rate identities at a fee of {{< var pricing.fee_probe >}} on every booked loan,
on every `verify.py` run, and fail if a residual reaches the unit tests' tolerance
({{< var pricing.identity.fee >}}). That check catches the waterfall and the rate solvers
disagreeing about the fee; it cannot catch a fee mishandled consistently in both — doubled,
say — which only a test with a known answer would. The book-level functions have no interim
control beyond `verify.py`'s summary comparison. **Owner:** pricing tool developer.

## Finding 5 — The market assumptions have no owner, and one dominates {#pr-finding-5}

**Finding.** The seven values that set every rate in this chapter are a dict in a
configuration file. Nothing records who owns each, when it was set, or why; and the one with
the largest effect on the outcome, the cost of funds, is the one most exposed to the funding
market.

**Evidence.** `shared/config.py::MARKET` holds the seven values with a one-line comment each,
and no owner, effective date or change log ([6.4](assumptions.qmd#pr-market)). The values
have not changed since `stage-1` ([6.9](gate.qmd)). Of the six assumptions stressed by
{{< var pricing.sens.step >}} ([6.6](sensitivity.qmd)), `cost_of_funds` moves the share
clearing furthest: from {{< var pricing.share_clears >}} to
{{< var pricing.sens.cost_of_funds.up.share_clears >}} (+{{< var pricing.sens.step >}}) or
{{< var pricing.sens.cost_of_funds.down.share_clears >}} (−{{< var pricing.sens.step >}}). The
same dict also feeds the data generator's quotes and line increase's gate
([6.4](assumptions.qmd#what-a-change-to-one-moves)).

**Impact.** Pricing has no estimated parameters ([D0](../d0-summary.qmd#why-pricing-is-listed-as-a-tool-not-a-model));
its risk lives in its inputs, and these are the inputs it owns. D0 says they are "set and
changed through change control (D9) like any other policy value". The control that exists
is code review of `shared/config.py`: it would show *that* a value changed, not who decided
it, on what evidence, or what it moved. A change to the cost of funds of the size a funding
market can deliver moves several percentage points of the book across the hurdle, and moves
D8's gate at the same time.

**Compensating control.** Name an owner for each assumption — the proposals are in
[6.4](assumptions.qmd#pr-market) — and keep a dated change log with the reason for each
change. Before a changed value is used, re-run [6.5](performance.qmd) and
[6.6](sensitivity.qmd) and D8's gate, and have the owner sign off the result. Until then two
controls apply: `verify.py` recomputes the `market.*` facts from `MARKET` on every run and
fails until the facts are rebuilt, so no change reaches `main` unseen
([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd)); and every change is a commit that states what was verified
([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd#stage-tags-and-change-control)). **Owner:** pricing tool
owner, with Treasury and Finance (all proposed; to be named).

## Observations {#pr-observations}

Recorded but not raised as findings. Each is a design choice stated here so it can be
challenged, minor on this data, or covered by a control above.

| Observation | Evidence | Why not a finding | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| The workbench and the batch price on PDs computed over different rows | The workbench scores all {{< var score.n_applicants >}} applicants at start-up; `price_population` scores the {{< var pricing.n >}} booked alone. The PDs differ by {{< var pricing.whatif.pd_max_diff >}}, and the verdicts differ on {{< var pricing.whatif.flips >}} loans ([6.5](performance.qmd#pr-whatif)) | Bounded below the engine tests' tolerance, with no verdict changed; a property of the scorecard's batch prediction, not of pricing | The facts assert the bound and the flip count on every run; a breach fails `verify.py` |
| The recommended rate earns well above the hurdle | It is the hurdle-clearing rate plus the base margin; the worked example's ROE at its recommended rate is {{< var pricing.example.roe_at_recommended >}} against a {{< var market.roe_hurdle >}} hurdle ([6.3](methodology.qmd#pr-recommended)) | A design choice, documented in the code as a "cushion" | Read the hurdle-clearing rate, not the recommended rate, as the minimum that earns the hurdle (a prohibited use, [6.1](purpose.qmd#prohibited-uses)) |
| `capital_ratio` and `roe_hurdle` are one assumption for the verdict | Moving either by {{< var pricing.sens.step >}} gives the same clearing count, {{< var pricing.sens.capital_ratio.up.n_clears >}} up and {{< var pricing.sens.capital_ratio.down.n_clears >}} down ([6.6](sensitivity.qmd)) | Algebra: they enter the test only as a product | Their owners agree a change to either together (finding 5) |
| The mispriced share varies by industry | From {{< var pricing.worst_industry_rate >}} ({{< var pricing.worst_industry >}}) to {{< var pricing.best_industry_rate >}} ({{< var pricing.best_industry >}}) ([6.5](performance.qmd#by-industry)) | Industry is a structural zero in the generator: the spread is noise | None. Do not act on industry-level mispricing from this data |
| A loss is credited tax at the full rate | `tax = pre_tax × tax_rate`, negative for a loss ([6.4](assumptions.qmd#pr-simplifications)) | Changes how negative a loss-making loan's ROE is, not whether it is negative or whether a loan clears | Revisit with the other simplifications before any real use |
| The quoted rate is on the leakage deny-list and pricing reads it | `risk_based_rate` is in `LEAKAGE_COLUMNS`; pricing compares it with the engine's rates ([6.2](data.qmd#pr-quoted-rate)) | The deny-list governs model features; pricing has none, and the quote never sets a rate the engine produces | None; what the quote inherits from the generator is finding 1 |
